note: Tide-pool spots on the Tide pools page (living/?g=tidepools), written for Lookout; edit freely. Each spot's tide station is NOAA's nearest (Botanical Beach uses Neah Bay, across the strait; Canada's own predictions are at tides.gc.ca). Coordinates from OpenStreetMap; check them before relying on them.

spots.name: Botanical Beach
spots.where: Juan de Fuca Provincial Park, BC
spots.note: Sandstone shelves full of pools, studied by botanists since 1901. One of the richest on the coast.

spots.name: Wickaninnish Beach
spots.where: Pacific Rim National Park Reserve, BC
spots.note: Rocky points at either end of the long beach; tides from Canada's tables at tides.gc.ca.

spots.name: Point of Arches
spots.where: Shi Shi Beach, Olympic National Park, WA
spots.note: Sea stacks and arches with pools beneath them, at the end of the Shi Shi walk. Makah recreation pass needed.

spots.name: Salt Creek
spots.where: Tongue Point, near Port Angeles, WA
spots.note: Tongue Point is a marine sanctuary: anemones, sea stars and kelp on the Strait of Juan de Fuca.

spots.name: Rialto Beach
spots.note: Walk north about a mile and a half to Hole-in-the-Wall, passable at low tide, with pools around the sea stacks.

spots.name: Ruby Beach
spots.note: Sea stacks and driftwood; pools on the rocks at the north end at low tide.

spots.name: Rosario Beach
spots.note: Pools on Rosario Head, an easy walk from the parking. Sheltered from the open ocean.

spots.name: Lincoln Park
spots.note: City tide-pooling on Puget Sound: sea stars, moon snails and crabs on a minus tide.

spots.name: Haystack Rock
spots.note: A protected marine garden at the foot of the rock; tufted puffins nest on it from spring to summer.

spots.name: Hug Point
spots.note: Pools, a waterfall onto the beach, and an old road cut into the point, all reachable only at low tide.

spots.name: Yaquina Head
spots.note: Pools and a cobble beach below the lighthouse, with harbor seals on the rocks.

spots.name: Otter Rock
spots.note: A marine garden on the rocks beside the Devil's Punchbowl.

spots.name: Seal Rock
spots.where: Seal Rock State Recreation Site, OR
spots.note: Basalt rocks with pools and sea anemones; seals and sea lions offshore.

spots.name: Cape Perpetua
spots.note: A marine garden by the Devil's Churn and the Spouting Horn.

spots.name: Strawberry Hill
spots.note: Wide basalt benches with pools full of ochre stars, and harbor seals hauled out nearby.

spots.name: Cape Arago
spots.note: Coves below the cape with pools; sea lions and seals bark from Simpson Reef.

spots.name: Harris Beach
spots.note: Sea stacks and pools near the south end of the Oregon coast.

care: Step on bare rock, not on animals or seaweed; barnacles and mussels are alive.
Touch gently with a wet finger, or not at all. Never pull an animal off a rock.
Put back any rock you turn over, the same way up.
Take nothing living. Many spots are marine reserves where even empty shells stay.
Keep an eye on the sea and on the time: the tide comes back faster than you'd think, and so do sneaker waves.
